findings.problem: about and the by_org_id index cite `resolveRecipientSafeInTx`, but no function has that name. The Organization-recipient reader is `resolveRecipientSafe`.

about said `request`, `intent`, `deliveredAmount`, `attention`, `bridgeRefusal`, `resolvedBy`, `observationContext` and `cancelReason` were 'summarized as Unknown or String', but none of them is in the struct. It also left out the conversion, a writer outside the door.
key [payoutId, version] is not unique. A refusal line records the version that refused, so several refusals at one version share the pair. Changed key to [_id] and said so in about.

key [orgId, authUserId] is not unique. The table has no member id, authUserId is optional and nullable, and one person can hold several rows over time; readers take the first active row. Changed key to [_id].
`delivery` was booked as Unknown, but it is a closed union of 4 literals. about also listed it as summarized.

The union of two row shapes was booked wrongly. `userOpSenderSafe` was required, but the invitation shape does not have it. `purpose` was Unknown, but it is 4 literals. The by_eoa_sender and by_eoa_nonce indexes named eoaChainId, eoaSender and eoaNonce, which were not in the struct. organizationSafe and rolesModule, which both shapes have, were optional.

about said the escrow, receipt-history and observation columns 'are listed', but 17 columns were missing, among them invoiceEscrowCheckedAt, which the by_invoice_escrow_state index uses. tenancy was 'person' although an Organization can issue a row, which breaks the file's own rule that a mixed table uses 'organization'.
invokes was empty, but the function calls partyById and partyBySafeAddress, and both are booked in this file.
errors listed INVALID_INPUT, but no path throws it. The org branch throws UNKNOWN (organizationPartyMissing), and a destination with no Party falls back to its address.

about compared the block with 'the block it was added at'. The code compares it with row.startBlock.

Did not invoke accounts.require-payment-account-in-tx (issuerActorRef) or parties.party-by-safe-address (invoicePublicSummary through assertInvoiceOpen).

emits was empty, and about said vocabulary.ts has no payroll_run_transitioned. vocabulary.ts now exports event_payroll_run_transitioned, so I linked it.

state was a String, but judgedState returns the approval-state vocabulary.
via and reverseVia were Strings, but they are the closed ContactVia vocabulary.
about said 'the Payment views' call it. In payments only notices/reads.ts does; the other callers are Books, Access and Accounts.

findings.record: Requests/Payroll/Documents/Banking procedures that call back into payments
findings.problem: Calls back into payments' own door are named in about but not linked. procedures.ts imports neighbors.ts, so a link back would be a circular ESM import (TDZ at load). Affected: preparePaymentCommandInTx, replayRequestPaymentApprovalInTx, isPayrollBatchSettledInTx, readOrganizationPaymentBatchFactsInTx, captureMemoConflictRemovalInTx, voidedByLandedVoidInTx and actorInventory. All of them exist in procedures.ts.
findings.evidence: books/as-is/payments/procedures.ts:108 imports ./neighbors.ts; requests/writes/approvals.ts:18-19; payroll/runs/writes/progression.ts:9; documents/writes/memos.ts:13; requests/reads/attempts.ts:16; requests/writes/receipts.ts:18

missing.why: All of these exist in procedures.ts, but neighbors.ts cannot import them: procedures.ts imports neighbors.ts, and the cycle would hit a TDZ error at load. Linking them needs lazy Refs (thunks) in packages/book, or a later file that books the neighbor procedures which call back into payments.

missing.ownerFile: neighbors.ts (outside its scope as written: Requests calls them, not payments)

Without these procedures their table writes are listed on the Requests procedures, and the build reports write-boundary for them.

missing.ownerFile: none by the conventions (other concepts' internal rpcs)
missing.why: Payments' actions run these other concepts' internal functions (access/features/guards.ts:137-147; payments/executions/external/recoveries.ts:93,94,144,148). CONVENTIONS gives no file ownership of rpcs outside payments.

designFindings: Payments reads six other concepts' tables directly and writes one: accounts (payments/views/recipients.ts:75, commands/writes/requests.ts:31), identities (views/recipients.ts:80), orgs (views/recipients.ts:88, commands/reads/recipients.ts:24), counterpartyDestinations (views/recipients.ts:109), financialDocumentLinks (reads/participants.ts:125) and paymentRequests (writes/births.ts:45,79). It inserts into Requests' invoiceCheckoutPayments (commands/writes/items.ts:210).

Neighbors read payments' tables directly, so moneyExecutions is in effect a shared table. Requests reads payments, paymentCommands and moneyExecutions (requests/reads/invoices.ts:48,98,106; reads/instructions.ts:44; reads/attempts.ts:107; writes/approvals.ts:143; writes/receipts.ts:242). Banking reads movements (banking/payouts/writes/refunds.ts:85). Documents reads paymentCommands (documents/reads/parties.ts:218). Payroll reads payments (payroll/runs/reads/notices.ts:54). Permissions reads moneyExecutions in 8 places (permissions/reads/commands.ts:149, reads/occupancy.ts:165,239, writes/abandonments.ts:86,117, writes/verifications.ts:36, configurations/reads/commands.ts:64, configurations/writes.ts:184). Accounts reads it too (accounts/approvals/guards.ts:26).

Payments has import cycles with four neighbors, and a Payment birth is owned by two concepts. Payments calls Requests' prepareConfirmedRequestInTx, which calls back into Payments' preparePaymentCommandInTx, replayRequestPaymentApprovalInTx, requirePaymentWriterEnabled, validateRelease, refuseStreams and scheduledAtFor (requests/writes/approvals.ts:18-26; also checkouts.ts:20, purchases.ts, reads/attempts.ts:16, writes/receipts.ts:18-19 for actorInventory and desiredAttributions). Documents imports payments' captureMemoConflictRemovalInTx (documents/writes/memos.ts:13). Payroll imports isPayrollBatchSettledInTx and readOrganizationPaymentBatchFactsInTx (payroll/runs/writes/progression.ts:9, runs/events.ts). Banking's door imports applyPayoutRailDeliveryInTx and readPayoutFundingInTx (banking/payouts/writes/door.ts:12-13).

Books' money-fact door takes payments' stored row, Doc<"payments">, as input and reads its shape through moneySides and isCommitment. It also imports a payments type (books/facts/writes/money.ts:16, :26, :98-103), so Books depends on Payments' storage schema.

Payroll's run state machine (draft, authorized, settled) is driven by Payments inside Payments' own transactions (payroll/runs/writes/progression.ts:1-6; payments/verifications/writes/submissions.ts:131, writes/settlements.ts:13, verifications/writes/history.ts:228). Payroll then asks Payments back whether the batch settled.

Requests and Documents cross each other's storage. Requests patches Documents' financialDocumentMovements directly (requests/writes/receipts.ts:152-161), and Documents reads Requests' paymentRequests (documents/reads/movements.ts:84-91). Requests also reads identities, orgs and accounts directly (requests/reads/documents.ts:43,53; reads/births.ts:41-55; writes/checkouts.ts:90; writes/purchases.ts:210).

The same identity fact has four uniqueness contracts. requirePaymentAccountInTx and accountIdForAuthUserOrNull take .first() (accounts/reads/identity.ts:43, :145), requireAccountSignerInTx takes .unique() (:117), and requireExactAccountIdentityInTx collects and refuses duplicates (:52-84). Requests' issuerRecipient takes .unique() on accounts directly (requests/writes/checkouts.ts:90-95).

The feature gate checked from an action is read in a query of its own (access/features/guards.ts:137-153), so the gate decision is not atomic with the writes the due-schedule send makes later (payments/schedules/operations/send-due.ts:20).

Banking's 'one door' to a payout has two writers that bypass it. classifyPayoutRefundInTx patches payouts directly (banking/payouts/writes/refunds.ts:36), and the conversion inserts payouts (banking/tables/payouts.ts:126). For non-payments sources the door also calls Payments' writer back (door.ts:249-251).

Business time is not passed through. Payments calls ensureLedgerParty, ensurePartyByAddress and recordContactEdges without `now`, so they fall back to the backendNow shim (parties/writes/ledger.ts:22-28, parties/writes/parties.ts:102-108; payments/writes/deposits.ts:74, writes/births.ts:237-243).
A global environment gate defined in payments is checked inside Requests and refuses with NOT_IMPLEMENTED (requests/writes/approvals.ts:163; payments/rules/records.ts:215-219; payments/errors.ts:34).

Error ownership is blurred. Permissions throws storedRowBroken naming payments' moneyExecutions table (permissions/reads/approvals.ts:117), and Banking names payments' table in storedRowBroken("payments", "railOperationId") (banking/payouts/reads.ts:153). Separately, readSubjectProposalInTx is a read exported from a writes module (organizations/proposals/writes.ts:196), which Permissions imports (permissions/allowances/reads/worn.ts:10).

Two tables have no usable business key. orgMembers has no member id and can hold several rows per person and Organization (organizations/tables/members.ts:10-45). payoutTransitions can repeat (payoutId, version) on refusals (banking/tables/payouts.ts:196-199).

I edited /home/user/capxul-next/books/as-is/payments/neighbors.ts in place. It still has 127 records, and no export name changed, so siblings' imports still resolve. - A script checked every was: path and line against /home/user/factory. All exist, including the new ones.

Scope:

- The 42 tables cover every direct cross-concept db access under payments (scanned by table name) and every table those procedures touch.
